extra.reason: Fixed on fix/bind-mark-to-review. review-pr now uses pr-cycle-start/pr-cycle-end against .claude/.review-pr-in-progress. The Stop gate honors both markers; only .review-in-progress licenses mark. 8 tests in stop-gate.bats pin the separation; verified end to end (pr-cycle-start then mark = exit 3, stop gate still passes).

Shipped on fix/bind-mark-to-review (4939a5d). mark requires the cycle-start marker; accept-state is the named human override; review-pr gets its own marker via pr-cycle-start/pr-cycle-end. Four review iterations, 397 tests (from 350), verified end to end here and independently on oakum. Follow-up cpl-dwq tracks making mark freshness-aware.
Fixed on fix/sentinel-union-hash: sentinel gains a union: line and check/match/status fall back to it when the index equals HEAD. 6 new bats cases; 403/403 green.

Fixed on fix/sentinel-enumeration-failure (PR #27, e6a0bff + b3833d2): every git call in the hash stream signals with exit 9, mapped to drift so hooks block; the stream is generated to a file and hashed separately so pipefail's rightmost-nonzero rule cannot mask the signal; build_scratch_index guards its rev-parse and ls-files calls. The block names the failing path and states that accept cannot clear it. 13 tests, each verified to fail against the previous release. Note: PR #27 is green and mergeable but NOT yet merged at close time.

Fixed on fix/bats-inert-assertions: added assert_contains/refute_contains/assert_matches to plugins/review-cycle/tests/helpers.bash (nonzero on mismatch, expected-vs-actual message, empty-argument guard, invalid-regex detection) and converted all 87 bare mid-body [[ ]] assertions across every suite — the helper option the issue leaned toward. Also fixed a second inert class the issue did not name: mid-body '! cmd' assertions are set -e-exempt on EVERY bash per POSIX, not just 3.2 — guarded ~21 sites in command-parse.bats and install-hook.bats with the house '|| false' idiom (refute-helper upgrade tracked in cpl-csf). helpers-assert.bats pins the enforcement property under /bin/bash including a mutation-verified proof test. Verified: 424 tests green via bin/run-bats; bash 3.2.57 and bash 5.2 (Docker) both confirmed; reviewer mutation testing tripped a failure for every corrupted assertion. Follow-ups: cpl-csf (idiom retirement + lint guard), cpl-fjs (consolidate helper copies).

Implemented on feat/verified-message-tier: Phase 6 of the review skill gains the verified-message tier with the empirical-verification gate (remedy fixes: reproduce, run the printed remedy verbatim, confirm it clears; factual fixes: check the claim per step 2), the Codex-only valve for locally-unreachable claims (one per cycle, not counted against max-iter, with spent-valve and Codex-ineligible fallbacks), draft-time recording of the verification line, and the consequential frontmatter/Phase 9/README edits. All four acceptance criteria verified by an independent spec-conformance trace of the okm-l57 replay (2 iterations + 1 valve pass). Deliberate deviation, since the issue text was internally contradictory on unverified remedies: resolved as 'neither verified (locally or against authoritative documentation) nor explicitly flagged for the valve' — the only reading under which AC3/AC4 hold. Reviewed across three cycle rounds (Codex low + code-reviewer), 12 findings fixed inline.

Implemented on test/retire-assertion-idioms. Item 1: refute() in plugins/review-cycle/tests/helpers.bash, strict on exit codes — only 1 is a clean false, so refute grep -q x missing-file fails loudly instead of proving nothing; rejects a zero-argument call. Item 2: all 25 '! cmd || false' sites and all 12 pipeline sites converted, preserving the -qF fixed-string vs -q regex distinction (the two 'permissionDecision: *deny' sites went to assert_matches, not assert_contains). Item 3: tests/bats-assertion-idioms.bats — three patterns, three failure branches, 15 tests. Item 4: darwin-conditional bash 3.2 pin, not the unconditional -eq 3 the issue warned against.

SCOPE DIVERGENCE, recorded deliberately: the issue scoped 'a two-pattern grep with no tail-position analysis'; the guard is ~308 lines. The estimate predated knowing this class of rule's failure modes. Six review rounds found it reports clean without looking in seven distinct ways: broken regex, zero files scanned, incomplete worktree walk (git --others warns and exits 0), stale index entry, signal-killed grep (137, no stderr), newline in a filename, and a non-UTF-8 byte under a UTF-8 locale. The controls are what separate a guard from a decoration — the same distinction cpl-lan was about. Extraction to bin/lint-assertion-idioms (cpl-6xz) resolves the size by making enumeration the caller's job.

Corrections made during review, recorded because each was a wrong call I made: (a) removed the per-file grep status check reasoning no test could kill the mutant — backwards; a signal-killed grep writes no stderr, so it was live coverage, restored with the test that kills it. (b) Claimed git ls-files makes a half-walk impossible — true of --cached only; --others walks the worktree and warns without failing. (c) Added a branch exclusion to the leading-bang pattern against a hypothetical false positive, which let 12 of the 25 retired sites back in; the spec check proved zero leading-bang lines exist in the tree, so the exclusion bought nothing. Reverted to the issue's blunt pattern. (d) Rejected one Codex finding on evidence: compound [[ ]] && [[ ]] lists are inert on bash 3.2, so flagging them is correct.

Verified: 449 tests green; shellcheck clean; plugin validate strict; every branch and pattern mutation-killable; patterns re-verified under /usr/bin/grep since this machine's grep is ugrep. Follow-ups: cpl-6xz (extraction), cpl-mqy (suppression marker), cpl-fjs (helper consolidation).

Implemented on feat/adversarial-review-questions. Both surfaces the issue named, coupled as it required.

Surface 1: skills/review/SKILL.md Phase 3 composes one falsifiable question per leg before spawning, with per-agent shapes derived from the diff, a guard that a question with no command behind it is still a topic, and a spawn prompt requiring the answer to cite what was run. The Codex leg is included, its question riding developer_instructions under the same no-double-quotes constraint as the brief.

Surface 2: the four fix-loop agents gained the matching generative technique — mutation testing, fault injection, differential comparison and oracle sweeps, constructing the invalid value — each framed against the existing empirical-verification rule the issue said must not imply it.

DESIGN BLOCKER, resolved differently than proposed. The issue asked for a carve-out spelling out a disposable copy with the target checksummed. I wrote that as a prose recipe and it was wrong three times: no baseline was ever captured; git status reports codes not content; git diff HEAD never sees untracked files; ls-files omits staged-only files and is cwd-scoped. A maintainability audit then measured the decisive fact — an empty commit leaves a status comparison byte-identical and moves only the anchor line, so the recipe could not detect the commit clause of the very rule it enforced. The recipe was therefore deleted, not hardened. Agents carry a four-line behavioral rule; the cycle snapshots review-sentinel current-hash plus git config --local --list in Phase 3, compares in Phase 4, and Phase 8 refuses to mark a contaminated tree. One site instead of four, and it covers the Codex leg, which never had containment at all.

Corrections made during review, recorded because each was a wrong claim of mine caught by measurement rather than reading: (a) the containment baseline did not work, three times over; (b) I claimed git ls-files covered untracked content when git diff HEAD does not see untracked files at all; (c) I claimed the snapshot covers Phase 7, which runs after the comparison and includes an agent that edits by design; (d) the agent rule asserted a backstop that does not exist in review-pr or in direct invocation, which makes an agent less careful rather than more; (e) the escape-hatch paragraph telling agents to use a per-project opt-out failed 3/3 in its natural forms and was deleted rather than repaired, since no technique needs version control in the scratch copy; (f) the bump file twice described machinery that had been removed under it.

Scope note: skills/review-pr/SKILL.md was changed though the issue names only skills/review/SKILL.md. Its REPORT-ONLY instruction forbade editing any file, which flatly contradicts a carve-out licensing scratch-copy perturbation; shipping the carve-out alongside a known contradiction was the worse option. Extending falsifiable questions to that path is cpl-qeb.

Verified: 449 tests green; plugin validate strict; markdownlint clean; containment byte-identical across all four agents; the anchor line confirmed to be HEAD, which is why a commit moves it and porcelain does not.

Follow-ups: cpl-2id (commit gate, promoted P1, next), cpl-dn3 (subagent scratch isolation and the evasion rule), cpl-2yn (re-scoped to the remaining coverage gaps), cpl-qeb (review-pr questions), cpl-k46 (upstream sync), cpl-7ph (agent markdown tiers as behavior).

Shipped on branch fix/commit-gate-scope. The gate now stands aside only when the command proves the commit lands in another repository, and gates the project whenever it cannot tell.

All four motivating failures are resolved: a tracker description quoting the phrase, a heredoc writing a setup script, the hyphenated plumbing verbs, and blocking in a scratch repo. The detection half also lands for the marketplace version-bump gate, since both share the lexer.

WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND, and it matters more than the fix: three rounds surfaced 28 verified bypasses, and every one was a regression introduced by my own first draft. Of fourteen shapes tested in round one, the pre-change code denied twelve. One mistake repeated — routing was built to prove a negative using a partial bash parser, with every gap in that parser failing toward allow. Round three narrowed it further: a grep that errored, an awk that died, a lexer that desynced, a target that would not resolve, all read as "no commit here". The single most damaging line was a sed -n 1p that collapsed both project roots to one, leaving the gate silently off in whichever root the session was not using. One bypass was created by an earlier fix of mine: neutering metacharacters inside quotes corrupted a -C path containing parentheses into one that does not exist, so the gate stood aside.

VERIFIED, not asserted: 512 bats passing and 0 failing; 56 adversarial corpus shapes; 14 fault-injection cases driven by PATH shims; shellcheck, markdownlint, plugin validate and version drift all clean. Mutation testing across three rounds, with every surviving check now carrying a killing test. Four mutants stay alive by design — each is defence in depth behind a guard that fires first, killable only by breaking a tool for one call site and not another.

CLAIMS OF MINE THAT WERE WRONG and were corrected: the file header called PARSE_GIT_COMMIT_RE the single definition of detection when detection uses the VERB variant; the parse_cd_count docstring described a leading-cd-only rule already replaced by the multi-hop walk; the deny message understated what routes; and the limitation note called the unnamed-runner case an over-block when it is the opposite — a runner outside the named list has its quoted body blanked, matches no fallback, and the commit it carries passes.

PROCESS MISSTEP worth recording: my first mutation run injected faults directly into the repository under review while two review agents were reading it. One caught it — three hook files changed mtime mid-run — and discarded its first probe. Fault injection belongs on a PATH shim or a copy. The three follow-up issues carry that requirement in their acceptance criteria.

KNOWN AND DELIBERATE: acceptance criterion one is met when a command names the scratch repo, not when the session cwd simply is one. Verified pre-existing against HEAD, and a consequence of treating the cwd repo as a project root, which is what stops a stale CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR from disarming the gate where you are working. The in-repo opt-out the issue asked for now works. Commands over 32 KB skip the skeleton and let the raw text decide, which blocks rather than passes. The shell-invoker list is a named set, so python3 -c and similar runners are missed and the commit they hide passes; the gate has never claimed to be an adversarial boundary.

Follow-ups filed: cpl-3b0 (read the command prefix once instead of four times), cpl-6w9 (move the unfollowable-path predicate into the lexer lib), cpl-ttx (both gates resolve a target through one function; blocked on the other two). All three were deferred deliberately: the same audit proved this harness can be green and wrong for exactly this code, so refactoring the most bypass-prone code in the plugin on the strength of it, while rewriting the tests that pin its behaviour, is the wrong order.

Shipped on branch feat/evidence-requires-a-run. A claim about what a command does now cites a run of that command, and a declaration is never evidence for behavior.

The rule already existed but bound only fix authors, said nothing to reviewers, and never said a manifest is insufficient. It is now a third embedded policy beside comment and fix-vs-defer, and it reaches every leg: seven bundled agent bodies, the intent brief both review and review-pr compose for the Codex leg which has no body, the standalone reference copy, and the init skill that installs them. An unexercisable claim is resolved by an ordered two-outcome rule — first match wins, so a measurement skipped for budget keeps its place labeled inferred, and only a claim that was never runnable here and that no authoritative documentation settles becomes a question.

WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND. Two rounds, eighteen findings. The worst was self-refuting: the anchor example of the policy was itself never run. The sentence said doctest equals false does not stop cargo test --doc from compiling the crate; measured, cargo runs the doctests too, and the flag only removes them from plain cargo test. It had been replicated into seven runtime prompts and the changelog. Worse, iteration one's reviewer had already reported the doctests running and I did not act on it — a failure to extract evidence I had been handed, not a failure to have it.

Round one also found the policy contradicting itself two lines apart, prescribing a downgrade and then forbidding it; the maintainability auditor told to prove behavior preservation empirically while being the only reviewer with no containment rule, in the one phase the integrity check does not cover, with the sentinel marked immediately after; a required cleanup report with no slot in either template; init appending policies unconditionally; the reference copy omitting the rule the embedded copy calls load-bearing; the inline cleanup path never seeing its own rules; and review-pr's operator unbound while being the leg that posts publicly. Round two found four more, two of them defects in round one's fixes: my custom containment paragraph stated cycle-only facts flatly in a context where review-pr makes them false, and a summary field I added had no producer wiring it. Also that init's heading test misfires on an import-only CLAUDE.md — verified on this machine, where the policies live in an imported AGENTS.md, so the check would have appended duplicates of two already-active policies and defeated the upgrade path the release advertises.

VERIFIED: 512 bats passing and 0 failing; claude plugin validate strict; markdownlint clean; every skill under the line budget; the doctest correction measured locally on cargo 1.94.1 rather than taken from the reviewers; the ordered two-outcome rule checked against a decision table that now yields exactly one outcome per case, after Codex proved with its own table that the previous wording yielded two.

WHY THE LOOP STOPPED AT TWO. Findings were converging in scope, not count — round one found design holes, round two found detail. The dominant remaining risk was the prose I write each round rather than undiscovered design flaws: seven claims of mine turned out false this session, so each iteration closed findings and opened new surface, and two of round two's findings were defects in round one's fixes.

KNOWN GAP, and the reason the next cycle should differ: every reviewer this session loaded the installed 0.14.0 agent bodies, which do not carry this policy. They had the rule only because it was pasted into each prompt by hand. So the artifact itself has never been exercised — only a paraphrase of it. Run the next cycle with the plugin loaded from the working tree, or after this release lands, so the agents carry the rule themselves.

Follow-up cpl-x29 remains open and is the natural next task: detect a review leg whose commands could not execute and label it static-analysis-only. This issue deliberately did not touch that — cpl-gme binds what counts as evidence, cpl-x29 detects when a leg had none available.

Publish step derives each plugin's tag from its manifest version and publishes only that release when it is still a draft. Verified against nine shimmed states plus a read-only dry run using real gh, git, and manifests.

Every reviewer opens with a two-line execution receipt; both skills grade each reporting leg from it as executed, partial, static-analysis-only, or unknown, and demote declaration-only external-tool claims. Verified across 12 receipt shapes and 10 mutations; a bats guard holds the contract across the eight files that carry it.
